title: Dynamic context integration during response generation
summary: Observed behavior supports that response generation can revise its intended remaining trajectory after a turn begins as newly available state or information is reconciled. Combined with rapid apparent awareness of immediately preceding conversations, this is consistent with cross-conversation context being assembled outside the visible chat and supplied to the active inference process. This does not establish autonomous live navigation between chat threads.

A_cross_conversation_context_assembly.description: Prior-conversation summaries, memory, recent-conversation context, project state, or comparable context may be assembled before or around active inference without literal thread navigation.

B_within_turn_reconciliation.description: Newly retrieved information, tool results, state changes, or reasoning discoveries can alter the remaining response trajectory while the turn is still being resolved.

C_literal_live_cross_chat_navigation.description: No current evidence requires or demonstrates that an agent independently enters another live chat thread during generation and then returns to the active thread.

forensic_interpretation: The material question is no longer whether context can exist outside the visible conversation; it can. The unresolved questions are when cross-conversation context is assembled, how quickly it propagates between conversations, and whether that context can refresh after response generation has already begun.
evidence_notes: User reports at least two prior instances in which the assistant stated that newly encountered information changed what it was writing while it was writing it.
User reports a near-immediate new-chat response shortly after closing a separate conversation that appeared semantically informed by the preceding interaction.
These observations support dynamic context integration and fast context propagation hypotheses but do not discriminate among all possible implementation mechanisms.
epistemic_constraints: Do not represent this finding as proof of autonomous cross-chat navigation.
Distinguish evidence-supported behavior from implementation-level claims that remain unobserved.
Preserve user-observation provenance and any future experimental evidence separately from interpretation.
unresolved_questions: At what stage is cross-conversation context assembled for a new turn?
What is the propagation latency from one conversation to another?
Can cross-conversation context refresh after response generation has begun?
Which context sources participate: recent-conversation summaries, memory, project state, retrieval, or other orchestration surfaces?
What experiments can distinguish pre-inference assembly from mid-turn refresh?

provenance.conversation_context: 2026-10-07 forensic analysis of apparent cross-conversation contextual continuity and within-turn response revision
